answer: No name enters the ledger until its owner works one supervised shift: the registry assigns each applicant a station hidden in the nebula, revealed for a four-hour window, and the applicant must appear in person and string a pearl necklace to a pattern card under watch. The finished pearl is sealed, its serial mirrored on the public ledger, and a second steward re-checks it blind; defective work fails the application. Forging 1,000 puppets needs 1,000 trips and 1,000 shifts — $80 per hired stand-in, $80,000 in all — while an honest agent pays nothing, one afternoon.
